bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Hourly to Annual Pay

If you're paid by the hour or considering a salary offer, you'll often need to convert your hourly rate to an annual figure. The standard formula is simple: multiply your hourly rate by the hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, that's **hourly rate × 38 × 52**. This gives your gross annual salary before tax, super, and any deductions.

But real pay is more than just this number. You need to consider the National Minimum Wage, award rates, casual loading, tax brackets, and superannuation. And if you're wondering **can I salary sacrifice a car**, that's another layer that affects your take-home pay and tax position.

### The National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage each year. From 1 July 2026, it is **$26.44 per hour** for full-time and part-time employees, or **$1004.90 per week** for 38 hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making it **$33.05 per hour**. This is the legal minimum for employees not covered by an award or agreement.

However, most Australian workers are covered by a modern award or enterprise agreement, which often pays more than the minimum. Award rates vary by industry and classification. For example, a retail employee may have a higher base rate than the National Minimum Wage. If you're on an award, your hourly rate is set by that award, not the minimum wage. Always check your award or agreement to confirm your correct rate.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

Casual employees get a 25% loading on top of their base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. This loading is included in the casual rate you see. When using our [timesheet](/), you can tick a checkbox to add the 25% casual loading to your base hourly rate. Do not type a rate that already includes casual loading – the tool adds it for you.

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is **12%** of your ordinary time earnings, up to a maximum contribution base of **$270,830** per year. This means if you earn $100, your employer must pay an extra $12 into your super fund. Super is not deducted from your pay; it's an additional cost for the employer.

### Fortnightly Pay and Annual Conversion

Many employees are paid fortnightly. To find your gross fortnightly pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. For a 38-hour week at the National Minimum Wage, that's $1004.90 × 2 = $2009.80 per fortnight before tax. If you're on a higher award rate, use your actual hourly rate in the formula.

### Tax and Medicare Levy

Your annual gross pay is taxed according to the 2026–27 resident tax rates:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus, a Medicare levy of 2% generally applies (with reductions for low-income earners). The tax-free threshold is included in these rates. If you have a HELP debt or are liable for the Medicare levy surcharge, additional amounts may apply. Our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page can help you estimate your net income.

### Can I Salary Sacrifice a Car?

Yes, salary sacrificing a car is a common way to reduce your taxable income. Through a novated lease, your employer deducts car lease payments and running costs from your pre-tax salary. This lowers your assessable income, so you pay less tax. However, it also reduces the base for your super guarantee (since super is calculated on ordinary earnings after salary sacrifice). The ATO caps the tax-free portion of certain fringe benefits, so not all of the sacrifice is tax-free. Always get professional advice before entering a salary sacrifice arrangement, as it affects your overall financial position.

### Average Earnings and Comparisons

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports Average Weekly Earnings. For May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings were **$2083.70 per week**. All employees (including part-time) averaged **$1579.20 per week**. These are averages, not medians for any specific job. Your own pay may differ based on your industry, experience, and location.

### Using Our Tools

Our [reference tables](/data) provide quick conversions for common hourly rates. The [pay guides](/blog) section explains award coverage. For a detailed estimate of your annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay including tax and super, use our [timesheet](/). It assumes a consistent 38-hour week unless you change the hours. Remember, this is an estimate – it does not include unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
